_about: The one hand-written thing behind Name the Place. Every puzzle in
games/name-the-place/deck.js is DERIVED from this list by
`at` is [longitude, latitude], GeoJSON order, and is the ONLY thing that
decides which map a place is asked on. The deck DOES carry an extent
field, but it is derived from `at` at generation time by atlas.fits and
re-verified by a test - it is never written by hand here or there. A
hand-written extent would be a second source of truth for something the
coordinate already decides, and it invites a map drawn with no pin on it.
_rule: The location must not be seriously disputed. Where a site is argued over,
it is left out rather than guessed at: a confident wrong pin on a church
projector is worse than not having the place.

_excluded.why: several rival mountains and no consensus; Jebel Musa is tradition, not evidence
the distance in Luke 24:13 varies by manuscript and no site fits all readings
the identification with et-Tell is contested on dating grounds
a traditional site, never located in the text
its location is genuinely unknown: Spain, Sardinia and others are all proposed
13.9 units from Ephesus on the wide map; Ephesus is far more recognisable, so Miletus is the one that goes
9.8 units from Lystra on the wide map; one of the two can be asked, not both
its site was disputed (Kerti Huyuk against Devri Sehri) until an inscription settled it, and it sits in the same Lycaonian cluster as Lystra and Iconium, as the least known of the three
off the edge of the wide map (east of 47.5 degrees), so it cannot be shown

places.note: Genesis says the mountains OF Ararat, plural: the highland the Assyrians called Urartu, not one peak. The pin sits on the great massif that carries the name, which anchors the NAME only. It does not claim the ark's resting place (a rival site, Cudi Dagi, has an old tradition of its own), and the clue says somewhere in the highlands for that reason.
